text:
sara (support): Customer reported intermittent 429s on Dedicated. They say some traffic is mysteriously hitting shared pools.
kevin (acct): Started ~2026-03-10 13:02 UTC. Latency increased then 429s. No client config changes on their side.
kevin (acct): curl sample they used:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'x-redwood-tenant: acme-co' \
  -H 'x-redwood-tier: ["gold"]' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-7x","input":"hi"}'
```
sara (support): Notable: their Edge proxy rewrites single header into a JSON array string for some routes, so x-redwood-tier arrives as a bracketed JSON string.
monitor-bot: Alert: DedicatedPoolThrottleRate exceeded (pool: gold-dedicated-1) at 2026-03-10T13:05:11Z
lina (oncall): Router logs show many requests matched to default-shared with reason="tier-mismatch". Example: `route_decision tenant=acme-co tier_header='["gold"]' matched_policy=DEFAULT`.
jia (infra): That points to control-plane normalizer not handling JSON-encoded array headers. Can we get raw request headers as seen by control-plane for a repro request?
oliver (runtime): Also watch for header-merge behavior: if multiple same-name headers are joined with commas, a JSON array could become '["gold"],something' and break equality checks in the selector.
sara (support): Control-plane trace sample: `x-redwood-tier: "[\"gold\"]"` (single header containing a JSON array string). Our selector is `header:x-redwood-tier == 'gold'` so it doesn't match.
kevin (acct): Repro I ran on staging:
1) Route through their Edge that JSON-encodes the tier header.
2) Send 200 requests.
Result: ~90% go to gold-dedicated, ~10% fallback to default and start hitting 429s. Can repro reliably on staging.
jia (infra): Please repro and include X-Request-Id so we can stitch router -> control-plane -> pool decision traces.
kevin (acct): Sent staging trace for X-Request-Id r-9f2c1. Logs pasted into the thread.
oliver (runtime): Pulled r-9f2c1. Normalizer saw header_raw='["gold"]'. Code path: split_on_commas(header_raw) -> returns ['["gold"]'] (no commas). Later evaluator expects plain token 'gold'. We never JSON-unquote the single string wrapper. Missing parse step.
sara (support): Summary: control-plane header parsing regressed for JSON-array-style headers. Result: tier selector mismatch -> fallback to shared pool -> noisy-neighbor throttling on shared.
lina (oncall): What are immediate mitigations? Patch will take some time.
jia (infra): Short-term workaround: create tenant-affinity override rule for tenant acme-co to pin to gold-dedicated until fix is deployed. Also throttle rate-limit the fallback pool for that tenant to avoid shared saturation.
kevin (acct): Added tenant override in staging and applied a temporary rate cap on default-shared for acme-co. Customer reports 429s stopped, latency back to normal.
oliver (runtime): Working on hotfix: cp/normalize-header-json-array-fix. Plan: attempt JSON parse if header value starts with '[' or '{', extract first string token and normalize. Added unit tests for x-redwood-tier variants (`gold`, "gold", `["gold"]`, `gold,other`).
oliver (runtime): Intend to roll patch to control-plane canary tonight (00:30 UTC), monitor for misroutes for 30m, then promote. Will also add a small regression test to e2e routing harness.
jia (infra): Post-deploy tasks: run synthetic for acme-co header variants, verify X-Request-Id traces map to gold-dedicated consistently, and remove tenant override once stable.
sara (support): Noted. I'll keep customer updated and mark this P2 until fully resolved. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
lina (oncall): Follow-ups: add an observability alert for sudden jumps in "tier-mismatch" reasons in route_decision logs so we catch regressions earlier.
kevin (acct): Customer happy with workaround. Will notify if they revert Edge change, but asked us to fix on our side.
monitor-bot: Incident note appended to ticket INC-2026-0310-56.
